title: Synthetic engineering selfcheck of the owned native factory
problem: Exercise the project's existing factory contract against its controlled implementation and tests without inventing human acceptance or live source coverage.
non_goals: No real source acquisition, model/provider calls, installation, publication or deployment.
No native host qualification or genuine end-user approval claim.
No automatic independent review or learning activation.
This synthetic fixture is not an accepted brief.

limitations: Knowledge locators, revisions and repeated hex digests are explicit synthetic schema fixtures, not real source citations or content hashes.
No actual wiki or authoritative repository comparison is established by these knowledge fields; current live coverage is NOT_ASSESSED.
Actual controlled candidate bytes and check observations are bound by the runner at execution time, separately from these synthetic source claims.
The engineering harness's synthetic decision is not human acceptance, and no independent review is pre-recorded.

reuse.rationale: Exercise the existing project-owned factory through its real core regression command rather than introduce a duplicate runner; the source-reference envelope is explicitly synthetic.

acceptance.behavior: At least 43 core cases exercise strict specs, exact decisions, actual check processes, missing/foreign/stale evidence, negative review, candidate changes, repair, finite attempts, cancellation and explicit reconciliation.

argv: import sys,unittest; suite=unittest.defaultTestLoader.discover('tests',pattern='test_native_factory.py'); count=suite.countTestCases(); assert count>=43, 'Missing core acceptance cases'; result=unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=1).run(suite); ok=result.wasSuccessful() and result.testsRun==count and not result.skipped and not result.expectedFailures; print('SPARKFORGE_CORE_ACCEPTANCE_COMPLETED' if ok else 'SPARKFORGE_CORE_ACCEPTANCE_FAILED'); sys.exit(not ok)
